MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING
  CITY OF NORWALK
  PUBLIC SAFETY COMMISSION
  March 3, 2025

Chair LeGaspi called the meeting to order at 5:58 p.m. in the Council Chambers, Norwalk
City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard, Norwalk, California. Responding to the roll call were
Chair LeGaspi, Commissioner Apodaca, Commissioner Hoskins, Vice Chair Rosoff,
Commissioner Dr. Rodriguez, Commissioner Greenidge and Commissioner Brizuela.
Also present were Richard Newton, Interim Director, Rita Ruiz, Public Safety Manager,
Public Safety Quadrant Officers Braulio Ortiz, John Cruz, Christopher Swanson, Horacio
Lozano, Stephanie Garcia, and Veronica Lomas, Management Analyst.

APPROVAL OF MINUTES

Vice Chair Rosoff motioned for the approval of the minutes of the Public Safety
Commission Meeting minutes that was held on February 3, 2025. Commissioner Apodaca
seconded the motion.

MOTION CARRIED BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

AYES:  Chair LeGaspi, Commissioner Apodaca, Commissioner Hoskins, Vice
  Chair Rosoff, Commissioner Dr. Rodriguez, Commissioner Greenidge
  and Commissioner Brizuela.
NOES:  None
ABSENT: Commissioner Peña and Commissioner Fernandez-Silva
ABSTAIN: None

REPORTS

Mrs. Lomas advised that the department will be providing an update on our new
Community Safety Partnership team. Mr. Newton reported that last month we appointed
our new Quadrant Officer team and reminded the Commissioners of the CSP teams
goals. The Quadrant Officers are to serve as ambassadors to the community. The city is
divided into four separate quadrants and the designated officer works with the businesses
in their assigned quadrant and the residents to improve quality of life concerns and serve
as the liaison between the Los Angeles Sherrif’s Department and the City of Norwalk
Code Compliance Department. The quadrant officers host our Neighborhood Watch and
Business Watch Meetings with the goal of lowering Part I crimes citywide.

Mr. Newton is introducing the new Quadrant Officers. Officer Garcia has been with the
department for a year and a half, and her roles include the administration side of the team
as well as covering quadrants as needed. Officer Garcia has a bachelor’s degree in
Criminology and Sociology as well as a master’s degree in Criminology. Officer Lozano
is the Quadrant Officer for Quadrant 4 which is south of Rosecrans Ave. and east of
Pioneer Ave. Officer Lozano has been with the department for a year and five months
 and has a bachelor’s degree in Criminal Justice and has a future goal of becoming a
police officer. Officer Swanson is the Quadrant Officer for Quadrant 2 which is north of
Rosecrans Ave. and east of Pioneer Ave. and has been with the department for a year
and eight months. He currently attends Cal State University of Dominguez Hills and is
finishing his last semester and obtaining his bachelor's degree. Officer Cruz oversees
Quadrant 3 which is west of Pioneer Ave and south of Rosecrans Ave. Officer Cruz has
been with the department for two years and has had the opportunity to work field patrol
as well as in the Office of Emergency Management. Officer Cruz has his bachelor's
degree in Criminal Justice from Cal State University of Fullerton. Lastly, Officer Braulio
Ortiz is the Quadrant Officer for Quadrant 1 which is north of Rosecrans Ave. and West
of Pioneer Blvd. Officer Ortiz has been with the department for over two years. Officer
Ortiz started on field patrol, became a shift lead and a field training officer.

Moving forward with the agenda, Interim Emergency Preparedness Manager, Jazmine
Salas provided a presentation on the Office of Emergency Management first quarter
highlights. The OEM upgraded the Mobile EOC which is deployed at City events to
enhance safety and emergency preparedness. There has been a total of 5 deployments
this quarter. There has been one Emergency Operation Activation for the Windstorm
Event that occurred in January. The EOC was activated for 24 hours with two operational
periods with Office of Emergency Management staff and field personnel deployed to
assist with keeping eyes on the city. The City of Norwalk is fortunate enough to have
trained staff and volunteers that were able to respond as mutual aid to assist during the
Pacific Palisades Fire and the Eaton Fire. OEM staff were deployed to assist Malibu EOC
for about a week. Norwalk was one of two CERT programs assisting with water
distribution at the Eaton Fire.

Some upcoming important launches for the Office of Emergency Management include
the WebEOC launch which is virtual critical event SharePoint which can help keep track
of different stakeholders that need to have an ongoing representation of what is occurring
during an event. Lastly, the Continuity of Operations Plan (COOP) that ensures essential
city functions remain operational during critical events. This helps establish what is
important to communicate to residents during a disaster.

STAFF COMMENTS

Mrs. Lomas went over the March 2025 calendar.

COMMISSIONER COMMENTS

Vice Chair Rosoff questioned whether the Quadrant officer team will be a rotating position
between officers in the department. Mr. Newton advised that it will be as this job is a
steppingstone for many officers.
 Commissioner Dr. Rodriguez requested clarification regarding WebEOC. Jazmine Salas
advised that it is a dashboard that important stakeholders can use during a disaster to
keep track of live updates on what resources are being used or requested. Any
Emergency Management staff within the city has access to this information as well as the
Los Angeles Sherrif’s Department.

Commissioner Dr. Rodriguez commented that she attended the Coffee with a Commuter
event and gave kudos to Officer Contreras and the Trainee on shift for being helpful and
friendly as she made herself familiar with the Transportation Center for a future train ride.

Vice Chair Rosoff asked if there will be any upcoming Coffee with a Quadrant event to
help the business owners as well as the community to get familiar with the new Quadrant
Officers. Mrs. Ruiz advised she is working on getting them scheduled and will be sure to
advise all Commissioners once a date has been confirmed.

Chair LeGaspi shows appreciation to the Quadrant Officers for working hard and giving
support for all that they do. He also mentions that there is now a left turn lane to enter the
Plaza on Pioneer and Firestone and he appreciates the follow-through to this concern
and making this happen.

ADJOURNMENT:

Being no further business to come before the Public Safety Commission, the meeting was
adjourned at 6:23 PM.

_______________________________
CHAIR
Richard LeGaspi
